title: handshake-and-backpressure-field-notes-nov09-2029
notes:
Purpose
Quick capture from the Friday field sync to record observed handshake/backpressure behaviors across recent load spikes, and to track follow-ups. This is a working log — not a full postmortem.

Attendees
- Aisha (note taker)
- Marco (kernel lead)
- Evelyn (SRE oncall)
- Samir (batching experiments)
- guest: Lina (infra perf) for 15m

Overview / Why we met
- Multiple customer routes saw transient 95th p99 latency regressions during the 11/06 afternoon burst. Root diff pattern pointed to delayed kernel handshakes combined with aggressive backpressure at the queue layer, which amplified micro-batching starvation.
- We wanted explicit, observable hypotheses and small experiments to validate: handshake timing variance, backpressure thresholds, and whether prefill eviction is worsening jitter.

What we observed (raw)
- Across 3 nodes during spike: handshake RTT increased from median 6ms -> 18ms on cold partitions. Cold partitions correlated with KV-prefill misses for long prefix keys from high-context chats.
- Backpressure trigger fired at queue length 120 (configured) while effective in preventing OOMs, it caused sudden drop in batching opportunities: microbatch size fell from average 8 -> 2 for ~120s.
- Prefill eviction was observed: shadow-cache eviction API showed 27% eviction rate during the burst window on node-3 (hot prefix churn). Evictions led to additional kernel roundtrips.
- Thermal throttling unrelated this time (checked GPU telemetry).

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Kernel handshake jitter is amplified by KV-prefill misses that cause additional synchronous IO during handshake path. If we move a lightweight prefetch earlier in the request pipeline handshake variance should fall. (Primary)
2) Backpressure thresholds tuned for steady-state burst suppression are too coarse for short high-QPS spikes; they kill batching too aggressively. A ramped backpressure policy could preserve short-lived batching. (Secondary)
3) Eviction policy LRU window is too small for conversational workloads with long-tail prefixes; raising the time-to-live for hot keys would lower misses. (Tertiary)

Data to collect (actionable metrics)
- handshake.rtt.{median,p95,p99} by partition and by prefill_hit=true/false (added tags to trace).
- queue.microbatch_size.avg and queue.microbatch_size.p95 during backpressure events.
- shadow-cache.eviction.rate and eviction.reason breakdown (size vs. ttl vs. explicit purge).
- per-request additional kernel-roundtrips count (instrument handshake->prefill path).

Short experiments (to run in canary pool)
1) Early-prefill probe: add nonblocking async prefetch call before handshake completes; if prefetch hits return immediately, otherwise allow handshake to continue but log timestamps. Canary: 10% traffic on dedicated canary node set. Owner: Marco. Target window: 2 days. Success metric: p95 handshake RTT down >= 15% and no change to p99 error rate. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/4128
2) Ramped backpressure: implement a backpressure curve that degrades accept probability over queue length 60..180 (linear) instead of hard cutoff at 120. Canary flag true for two pods in staging. Owner: Samir. Metric: average microbatch size during spike preserved above 4; tail latencies stable.
3) TTL tuning: on one canary partition increase hot-key TTL from 90s -> 300s; monitor eviction rate and memory pressure. Owner: Evelyn. Metric: eviction.rate drop >= 30% and memory usage < +8% delta.

Risks and caveats
- Early-prefill increases request work on entry path; must be strictly nonblocking or we risk adding p99 latency during prefill misses. Use async IO and cancelation if handshake finishes first.
- Ramped backpressure could temporarily allow higher memory pressure; need to combine with dynamic headroom checks. Add guard to abort ramp if aggregate mem > 92%.
- TTL bump might increase resident memory on GPU nodes; check historical memory tails and set emergency rollback if > 10% over baseline.

Immediate action items (owners + ETA)
- Marco: prototype early-prefill async stub and add trace points for prefill_hit tags. Create PR + deploy to canary by EOD 2029-11-10.
- Samir: implement ramped backpressure config and feature flag; load test in staging, roll to canary 2029-11-11.
- Evelyn: carve canary partition, bump TTL config, and add eviction/reclaim dashboard tile; complete by 2029-11-11 morning.
- Aisha: update runbook section "handshake-degradation" with temporary mitigations and the rollback checklist. 2029-11-12.
- All: follow-up sync next Monday 2029-11-12 10:00 PT (15m).

Notes from quick infra check (Lina)
- Network egress path for node-3 had a 200ms spike to storage endpoint during the window. Probable contributor to prefill miss amplification. Lina to open infra ticket and ask cloud provider to correlate. Ticket: JIRA-RT-2987.

Observability tweaks (quick list)
- Add prefill_hit tag to request traces and top-level logs.
- Emit event when backpressure transitions from ACCEPT -> PROBATION -> REJECT to make offline analysis easier.
- Record per-partition handshake attempt counter (success/fail/timeout).

Longer-term work candidates
- Move prefetch path entirely off-critical handshake path; investigate shadow-prefetch + speculative KV warmup using lightweight LRU prediction models. (Research spike Q1 2030)
- Smarter eviction: workload-aware TTL and size heuristics per tenant to avoid global settings hurting tail workloads.
- Explore per-route adaptive backpressure tuned by model/sequence-length distribution rather than single global curve.

Misc notes and micro-decisions
- For canary flags: prefer feature-flag gate over env var to allow remote flip.
- Logging level for prefill misses should be INFO for now; we will sample full payloads at 1%.
- If canary experiments show memory > +8% but latency improves widely, discuss trade at Tuesday triage.

Appendix (raw timestamps)
- 2029-11-06 14:03:12 UTC: Node-3 queue length spike begins
- 2029-11-06 14:03:18 UTC: handshake rtt p95 begins climbing
- 2029-11-06 14:04:10 UTC: backpressure state enters REJECT briefly
- 2029-11-06 14:06:30 UTC: eviction rate spike observed (27%)
